passages.text: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid.
passages.sermon: A person who loves discipline also loves knowledge.\r\nA person who hates correction is foolish.
passages.original: אֹהֵ֣ב מ֭וּסָר אֹ֣הֵֽב דָּ֑עַת וְשֹׂנֵ֖א תוֹכַ֣חַת בָּֽעַר׃

passages.text: The good man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns a man who devises evil.
passages.sermon:
A good man receives favor from the LORD.
The LORD gives approval to the good man.
A man who plans evil faces condemnation from the LORD.
The LORD judges and condemns those who devise evil plans.
passages.original: ט֗וֹב יָפִ֣יק רָ֭צוֹן מֵיְהוָ֑ה וְאִ֖ישׁ מְזִמּ֣וֹת יַרְשִֽׁיעַ׃

passages.text: A man cannot be established through wickedness, but the righteous cannot be uprooted.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man cannot stand firm.
Wickedness cannot make a person secure.
A righteous person has a strong foundation.
No one can uproot the righteous.
The righteous remain steady and unshaken.
passages.original: לֹא־ יִכּ֣וֹן אָדָ֣ם בְּרֶ֑שַׁע וְשֹׁ֥רֶשׁ צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים בַּל־ יִמּֽוֹט׃

passages.text: A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown, but she who causes shame is like decay in his bones.
passages.sermon:
A wife with noble character brings honor to her husband.
She is like a crown on his head.
A wife who brings shame harms her husband deeply.
She is like decay in his bones.
passages.original: אֵֽשֶׁת־ חַ֭יִל עֲטֶ֣רֶת בַּעְלָ֑הּ וּכְרָקָ֖ב בְּעַצְמוֹתָ֣יו מְבִישָֽׁה׃

passages.text: The plans of the righteous are just, but the counsel of the wicked leads to deceit.
passages.sermon:
The righteous make plans.
Their plans are just.
The wicked give counsel.
Their counsel leads to deceit.
passages.original: מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת צַדִּיקִ֣ים מִשְׁפָּ֑ט תַּחְבֻּל֖וֹת רְשָׁעִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
passages.sermon:
Wicked people speak dangerous words.
Their words wait to harm others.
Upright people speak with honesty.
Their words save and protect.
The upright rescue others by what they say.
The wicked seek to hurt, but the upright bring safety.
passages.original: דִּבְרֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֱרָב־ דָּ֑ם וּפִ֥י יְ֝שָׁרִ֗ים יַצִּילֵֽם׃

passages.text: The wicked are overthrown and perish, but the house of the righteous will stand.
passages.sermon:
The wicked act with evil intent.
God overthrows the wicked.
The wicked perish.
The righteous live with integrity.
God establishes the house of the righteous.
The house of the righteous stands firm.
passages.original: הָפ֣וֹךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים וְאֵינָ֑ם וּבֵ֖ית צַדִּיקִ֣ים יַעֲמֹֽד׃

passages.text: A man is praised according to his wisdom, but a twisted mind is despised.
passages.sermon:
A wise man receives praise.
People honor him for his understanding.
A person with a twisted mind is despised.
People look down on him.
passages.original: לְֽפִי־ שִׂ֭כְלוֹ יְהֻלַּל־ אִ֑ישׁ וְנַעֲוֵה־ לֵ֝֗ב יִהְיֶ֥ה לָבֽוּז׃

passages.text: Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, than to be self-important but lack food.
passages.sermon:
A person may be lightly esteemed by others.
This person may have a servant.
Another person may act self-important.
This self-important person may lack food.
It is better to be lightly esteemed and have a servant.
It is worse to be self-important and lack food.
passages.original: ט֣וֹב נִ֭קְלֶה וְעֶ֣בֶד ל֑וֹ מִ֝מְּתַכַּבֵּ֗ד וַחֲסַר־ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: A righteous man regards the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are only cruelty.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man cares for his animal.
He understands its needs.
A wicked man shows mercy.
But his mercy is cruel.
His kindness brings harm.
passages.original: יוֹדֵ֣עַ צַ֭דִּיק נֶ֣פֶשׁ בְּהֶמְתּ֑וֹ וְֽרַחֲמֵ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים אַכְזָרִֽי׃

passages.text: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies lacks judgment.
passages.sermon:
A wise person works his own land.
He gains plenty of food.
A foolish person chases empty things.
He shows he has no sense.
passages.original: עֹבֵ֣ד אַ֭דְמָתוֹ יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־ לָ֑חֶם וּמְרַדֵּ֖ף רֵיקִ֣ים חֲסַר־ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: The wicked desire the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.
passages.sermon: A wicked person wants what evil people steal.\r\nA righteous person has a strong and growing foundation.\r\nThe righteous person flourishes.
passages.original: חָמַ֣ד רָ֭שָׁע מְצ֣וֹד רָעִ֑ים וְשֹׁ֖רֶשׁ צַדִּיקִ֣ים יִתֵּֽן׃

passages.text: An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble.
passages.sermon:
An evil man speaks rebellious words.
His own words trap him.
A righteous man faces trouble.
He escapes from it.
passages.original: בְּפֶ֣שַׁע שְׂ֭פָתַיִם מוֹקֵ֣שׁ רָ֑ע וַיֵּצֵ֖א מִצָּרָ֣ה צַדִּֽיק׃

passages.text: By fruitful speech a man is filled with good things, and the work of his hands returns to him.
passages.sermon:
A man speaks good words.
His words bring him good things.
A man works with his hands.
His work brings him a reward.
Each person receives good from his own words and actions.
passages.original: מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־ אִ֭ישׁ יִשְׂבַּע־ ט֑וֹב וּגְמ֥וּל יְדֵי־ אָ֝דָ֗ם יָשׁוּב לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to counsel.
passages.sermon:
A fool thinks his own way is right.
He trusts his own judgment.
He does not seek advice.
A wise man listens to counsel.
He values advice from others.
He learns from what others say.
passages.original: דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֱ֭וִיל יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְשֹׁמֵ֖עַ לְעֵצָ֣ה חָכָֽם׃

passages.text: A fool’s anger is known at once, but a prudent man overlooks an insult.
passages.sermon:
A fool shows his anger right away.
People see his anger immediately.
A prudent man hides his shame.
A prudent man does not show his anger.
A prudent man overlooks an insult.
passages.original: אֱוִ֗יל בַּ֭יּוֹם יִוָּדַ֣ע כַּעְס֑וֹ וְכֹסֶ֖ה קָל֣וֹן עָרֽוּם׃

passages.text: He who speaks the truth declares what is right, but a false witness speaks deceit.
passages.sermon:
A truthful person speaks honestly.
A truthful person declares what is right.
A false witness does not speak honestly.
A false witness speaks deceit.
passages.original: יָפִ֣יחַ אֱ֭מוּנָה יַגִּ֣יד צֶ֑דֶק וְעֵ֖ד שְׁקָרִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
passages.sermon:
Some people speak rashly.
Their words hurt like a sword.
Wise people use their tongues to heal.
Their words bring healing.
passages.original: יֵ֣שׁ בּ֭וֹטֶה כְּמַדְקְר֣וֹת חָ֑רֶב וּלְשׁ֖וֹן חֲכָמִ֣ים מַרְפֵּֽא׃

passages.text: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
passages.sermon:
Truthful lips last forever.
A person who speaks truth will endure.
A lying tongue lasts only a short time.
A person who lies will not last.
passages.original: שְֽׂפַת־ אֱ֭מֶת תִּכּ֣וֹן לָעַ֑ד וְעַד־ אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר׃

passages.text: Deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil, but the counselors of peace have joy.
passages.sermon:
People who plan evil have deceit in their hearts.
They hide lies and trickery inside.
People who give advice for peace have joy.
They feel happiness because they seek peace.
passages.original: מִ֭רְמָה בְּלֶב־ חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע וּֽלְיֹעֲצֵ֖י שָׁל֣וֹם שִׂמְחָֽה׃

passages.text: No harm befalls the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.
passages.sermon:
The righteous person does not suffer harm.
God protects the righteous from evil.
The wicked person is full of trouble.
Evil fills the life of the wicked.
passages.original: לֹא־ יְאֻנֶּ֣ה לַצַּדִּ֣יק כָּל־ אָ֑וֶן וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים מָ֣לְאוּ רָֽע׃

passages.text: Lying lips are detestable to the LORD, but those who deal faithfully are His delight.
passages.sermon:
The LORD hates lying lips.
Lying lips speak falsehood.
The LORD finds them detestable.
People who act with faithfulness please the LORD.
The LORD delights in those who are trustworthy.
passages.original: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה שִׂפְתֵי־ שָׁ֑קֶר וְעֹשֵׂ֖י אֱמוּנָ֣ה רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself, but a foolish heart proclaims its folly.
passages.sermon:
A shrewd man acts with wisdom.
He keeps his knowledge to himself.
A foolish person has a foolish heart.
A foolish heart speaks out its own folly.
passages.original: אָדָ֣ם עָ֭רוּם כֹּ֣סֶה דָּ֑עַת וְלֵ֥ב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים יִקְרָ֥א אִוֶּֽלֶת׃

passages.text: The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
passages.sermon:
A diligent person works hard.
A diligent person gains authority.
A lazy person avoids effort.
A lazy person becomes a servant.
Laziness leads to forced labor.
passages.original: יַד־ חָרוּצִ֥ים תִּמְשׁ֑וֹל ו֝רְמִיָּ֗ה תִּהְיֶ֥ה לָמַֽס׃

passages.text: Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up.
passages.sermon: Anxiety makes a man's heart heavy.\r\nA good word brings joy to his heart.
passages.original: דְּאָגָ֣ה בְלֶב־ אִ֣ישׁ יַשְׁחֶ֑נָּה וְדָבָ֖ר ט֣וֹב יְשַׂמְּחֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: A righteous man is cautious in friendship, but the ways of the wicked lead them astray.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man acts with caution in friendship.
He chooses friends carefully.
He avoids harm by being wise.
Wicked people follow their own ways.
Their ways lead them astray.
They do not choose friends wisely.
They end up in trouble because of their choices.
passages.original: יָתֵ֣ר מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ צַדִּ֑יק וְדֶ֖רֶךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים תַּתְעֵֽם׃

passages.text: A lazy man does not roast his game, but a diligent man prizes his possession.
passages.sermon: A lazy man does not cook what he catches.\r\nA diligent man values what he owns.
passages.original: לֹא־ יַחֲרֹ֣ךְ רְמִיָּ֣ה צֵיד֑וֹ וְהוֹן־ אָדָ֖ם יָקָ֣ר חָרֽוּץ׃

passages.text: There is life in the path of righteousness, but another path leads to death.
passages.sermon:
A righteous person chooses the path of righteousness.
This path gives life.
Another path exists.
This other path leads to death.
passages.original: בְּאֹֽרַח־ צְדָקָ֥ה חַיִּ֑ים וְדֶ֖רֶךְ נְתִיבָ֣ה אַל־ מָֽוֶת׃
